alex_w: Anyone else seeing `exports` conditional fields getting ignored when running the edge sample app in our monorepo + pnpm? import ends up as undefined in the edge worker but works locally with node.

maria_r: yup saw that earlier. weirdly only when package is symlinked by pnpm workspace. regular npm install doesn't reproduce it. :thinking_face:

ken_t: do you have a small repro? which bundler / dev server? vite/esbuild?

alex_w: repro is this repo: packages/edge-sample -> imports @infra/sdk. pnpm workspace links @infra/sdk -> packages/sdk. pkg.json in sdk has exports: { ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" } }

samir: same setup here. stack trace from edge runtime: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'createClient')` after `import { createClient } from '@infra/sdk'`. If I replace import with `const sdk = require('@infra/sdk')` it finds the cjs but then the edge runtime complains about .default shape. total mess.

maria_r: sounds like resolver is resolving to the package root (symlink) and then bundler doesn't read the package.json "exports" block because it sees the actual folder instead of the package entry. esbuild/vite behave differently from node resolver.

alex_w: here's the minimal stack log from vite build:

```
ERROR in ./node_modules/@infra/sdk/dist/esm/index.js
Module not found: Can't resolve 'buffer' in '/workspace/packages/edge-sample/node_modules/@infra/sdk/dist/esm'
```

which is bizarre because the file exists, it's just the import target seems wrong at runtime (undefined).

ken_t: two likely roots: pnpm's symlinks + Node's preserveSymlinks or the bundler resolving to realpath then not honoring package.json exports, OR the exports condition path not matching the bundler's expected environment (browser vs node vs default). For edge runtimes you often need a "browser"/"import" mapping.

samir: i tried patching package.json exports with explicit "./dist/esm/index.js": "./dist/esm/index.js" style entries and that made the import work in vite dev, but the actual deployed edge worker still pulled the CJS bundle.

maria_r: possible workaround: add an explicit "types" and an exports types path as well, e.g. "exports": { ".": { "import": { "types": "./dist/index.d.mts", "default": "./dist/esm/index.js" }, "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" }, "./*": "./*" } — bundlers often need the wildcard. Also try adding top-level "module" and "main" fields to aid older resolvers.

alex_w: tried adding module + main, still inconsistent. any pnpm flags we should try?

ken_t: try `nodeLinker=hoisted`? actually that changes how node_modules structure is written, but pnpm_defaults: `shamefully-hoist=true` can help. More relevant: Node's `--preserve-symlinks` behavior: if bundler resolves symlink to realpath it may pick a different package.json. There was also a bug where esbuild ignores package.json exports if the package is a symlink.

samir: i worked around it by publishing a local tarball and installing that (so not symlinked) — then everything resolved correctly. Not great for DX though.

alex_w: for the edge runtime specifically, do we need an "edge" conditional in exports? like "exports": { ".": { "edge": "./dist/edge/index.mjs", "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" } }

maria_r: yeah some bundlers look for a condition key matching their target. Vite's optimizer can set env to "browser" but our edge runtime bundler might use a different condition. Adding an explicit "edge" condition helped one of my packages.

ken_t: other quick hacks: in the edge-sample's vite config, alias `@infra/sdk` -> path.resolve(__dirname, '../sdk/dist/esm/index.js') for dev only, or add `optimizeDeps.exclude: ['@infra/sdk']` so it doesn't pre-bundle wrong. For builds, ensure your CI uses `pnpm install --shamefully-hoist` or use the tarball approach.

alex_w: thanks, i'll try aliases for dev. for CI deploy (private dedicated infra) we need a stable fix. maybe we should update our sdk's package.json to include a `exports` wildcard and an `edge` condition and add `types` explicitly. i'll open a tiny PR to expand exports entries.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy failed for edge-sample at 13:02 UTC — bundler error during build step: "Failed to resolve package @infra/sdk conditional exports". See CI #4823.

samir: @alex_w if you open the PR ping me, i've got a small script that validates exports against node/vite/esbuild conditions and will run it in CI.

alex_w: will do. quick action items: 1) PR to add `edge` conditional + wildcard exports + types to sdk package.json, 2) add a dev vite alias for edge-sample to avoid repro friction, 3) add CI test that installs via tarball to catch symlink-only regressions.

maria_r: awesome. small note: also consider documenting this in the monorepo onboarding docs — folks keep getting bitten by pnpm symlink vs published package differences.

ken_t: cool — thanks for the clear repro and notes. definitely file the PR and tag @samir.

alex_w: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1277 — includes examples of exports changes and a CI job that installs a tarball. pinged the thread. :rocket:

samir: reviewed and approved, small nit on ordering of fields. merged. feel free to revert if anything breaks.

alex_w: merged and verified in canary, edge-sample builds and imports fine now. marking this one as resolved. :party_popper:
